thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION in dedicated-reserved-pool-A (resv-north-1-A) — multiple enterprise reservations at 100% and queue length growing. paging oncall.
oncall-jamie: got it, I'm awake. joining bridge now. @sre-ryan you free?
sre-ryan: on my way, joining VC. initial metric: reserved GPUs used=128/128, queue_depth=2.3k, avg latency spiking 12s -> 95th 26s, errors: downstream 503s from router.
ops-maria: seeing heavy tail from tenant BrightBridge (resv bright-01) + a few smaller enterprise tenants. noisy sessions detected (long-running streaming sessions pinned to few GPUs).
eng-irma: likely noisy neighbor; autoscaler attempted scale up but node provisioning failed with cloud quota error. logs:
```
nodeprov: create_node failed status=429 body={"error":"PER_REGION_GPU_QUOTA_EXCEEDED"}
autoscaler: attempted +3 nodes but hit scale_limit=5 per-pool
```
prod-liz: BrightBridge on-call reported degraded API for their customers, high priority. CS alerted them.
customer-success-lucas: BrightBridge is seeing timeouts for checkout features. they are already on a reserved contract — we need mitigation ASAP.
oncall-jamie: immediate mitigations: 1) stop routing non-enterprise traffic to resv-north-1-A 2) apply per-tenant streaming timeout (cut existing long sessions to a safe threshold) 3) attempt temporary evictions for runaway sessions. I'll kick off (1) now.
eng-irma: recommended throttles: set tenant concurrency cap=8 for BrightBridge and 2 for medium tenants; live config change:
```
PATCH /config/pools/resv-north-1-A
set tenant_caps:{"bright-01":8, "mid-tier":2}
```
ops-maria: applying cap change... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
infra-bot: config patch succeeded, routing rule updated. non-enterprise routing diverted to shared-hosted pool.
oncall-jamie: good. second, evicting long-running streaming sessions older than 15m from pool. @sre-ryan please run drain script.
sre-ryan: running drain: `./scripts/drain-long-sessions --pool resv-north-1-A --age 900` -> found 112 sessions, evicted 96 (16 in finalizing state). logs show some stuck sessions tied to model variant gpt-embed-large.
eng-irma: that freed ~12 GPUs immediately, queue down to 1.7k, latency 95th -> 18s. still above SLO.
prod-liz: BrightBridge reports partial recovery but intermittent errors persist for heavy batched jobs.
oncall-jamie: autoscaler still failing to provision new nodes due to quota. @infra-bot can you request quota bump and also try different AZ?
infra-bot: raised cloud quota request via ticket #CQ-84921 to cloud provider; response ETA ~3h. attempted alternate AZ node create -> succeeded for one smaller instance type (A100->A10x) but our reserved pool is strict on GPU types; need fallback mapping.
eng-irma: we can remap a fraction of routing to fallback quantized model (gpt-compat-8q) that runs on smaller GPUs — lower perf but keeps BrightBridge alive. patching router to allow model fallback for enterprise override.
ops-maria: patch applied. rerouting 25% of BrightBridge traffic to compat-8q as emergency fallback.
customer-success-lucas: BrightBridge confirms error rate dropped ~40%, some degradation in response quality but critical flows OK. they're ok with short-term fallbacks.
prod-liz: we should open an incident bridge with account management and propose credit for customer and follow-up plan.
oncall-jamie: agreed. action items timeline:
- short (0-30m): apply caps + evictions + fallback remap (done)
- mid (30m-3h): quota approval / request alternate capacity / migrate some reservations to other pools
- long (>3h): permanent mitigation: autoscaler resilient to quota errors, better fallback mapping, noisy-tenant detection improvements.
sre-ryan: started a live chase on autoscaler code path. root cause: autoscaler treats 429 from cloud as transient and retries into a tight loop, hitting our internal rate limits and preventing clean backoff. will add exponential backoff and a circuit breaker for 429s.
eng-irma: quick patch to autoscaler backoff staged to canary. deploy bot:
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for autoscaler-backoff-2026.1 -> 5% traffic.
eng-irma: monitoring will watch provisioning attempts and pool free GPUs.
ops-maria: still seeing two noisy sessions that reappeared after evict -> investigating client reconnect patterns.
customer-success-lucas: maintaining communication with BrightBridge. scheduled 1:1 with their infra lead at +1h.
prod-liz: created follow-up ticket PROD-84922 (post-incident analysis + customer remediation + billing review).
oncall-jamie: escalation notes: possible config change by BrightBridge earlier? any recent canaries? @eng-irma
eng-irma: nothing from their tenant in change logs. most likely workload spike from a new internal batch job they rolled out overnight.
sre-ryan: mitigation status: queue 1.7k -> 1.2k after evictions + fallback, latency down to 14s at p95. autoscaler backoff patch in canary looks healthy so far.
oncall-jamie: interim customer message draft:
"We're actively mitigating a GPU capacity event affecting reserved pool resv-north-1-A. We've applied temporary caps and fallbacks; your critical flows should be restored. Our engineers are working on provisioning more capacity and a permanent fix. We will follow up with a timeline and compensation if needed."
customer-success-lucas: sending now.
prod-liz: please add a postmortem owner. assigning @sre-ryan.
sre-ryan: will own PM. early notes: noisy-neighbor detection thresholds too lax; autoscaler doesn't handle provider quota 429 gracefully; routing lacks per-tenant fallback mapping until now.
oncall-jamie: final for now — no full outage declared, but degraded for BrightBridge and some enterprise jobs. keep channel updated, escalate if queue stops dropping or new 429s appear.
eng-irma: scheduling post-incident retro. will prepare short-term PR for autoscaler backoff and a follow-up for fallback mapping UX in Console.
ops-maria: adding follow-up runbook steps to incident handbook: "If nodeprov 429 -> pause retries, mark pool degraded, trigger fallback model mapping" :memo:
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial_recovery. notifications sent to on-call rotation. incident channel will remain open for 2h for monitoring.
oncall-jamie: thx team. staying on watch for 2h. ping me if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
